claims.text: The superconducting critical temperature of HEA superconductors is primarily governed by effective valence electron count.
Introducing an f-electron element such as uranium causes pair breaking that suppresses Tc relative to an alloy with similar electron count but no f-electron element.
[TaNb]0.31(TiZrHf)0.69 and [TaNb]0.31(TiUHf)0.69 have disordered BCC structures.
Replacing Zr with U in the stated compositions maintains nearly the same overall valence electron count.
The controlled comparison should differ primarily by U-versus-Zr substitution while holding synthesis, processing, phase, and microstructural disorder comparable.
The comparison should be performed below approximately 10 K.
The uranium-containing alloy [TaNb]0.31(TiUHf)0.69 exhibits phonon-mediated superconductivity.
The (TaNb)1-x(ZrHfTi)x HEA family exhibits single-band isotropic s-wave superconductivity in the dirty limit.
A disordered BCC lattice itself sustains conventional s-wave, phonon-mediated superconductivity in these alloys.
Uranium-occupied lattice sites introduce additional scattering centers because of f-electron involvement.
Effective valence electron count governs the density of states at the Fermi level and the resulting electron-phonon coupling.
The density of states and electron-phonon coupling largely determine Tc in the proposed HEAs.
Uranium f-electrons cause scattering and pair breaking analogous to magnetic-impurity pair breaking.
Under matched conditions, the uranium-containing HEA should have a lower Tc than the Zr-containing counterpart.
Under matched conditions, the uranium-containing HEA should have a lower upper critical field Hc2 than the Zr-containing counterpart.
Tc in conventional Ta-Nb-Ti-Zr-Hf HEA superconductors evolves predictably with valence electron count.
Known HEA superconductors in the baseline family are broadly consistent with a BCS description and robust s-wave superconductivity.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to phonon-mediated, dirty-limit HEAs without dominant magnetic order, strong correlations, or major structural phase transitions.
The magnitude of uranium-induced Tc suppression may depend on microstructure and the local electronic environment.
Statistically indistinguishable Tc and Hc2 values for the matched U- and Zr-containing alloys would falsify significant uranium-induced pair breaking beyond the valence-electron-count prediction.
